agents.name: Dockerfile Cache Optimization
agents.summary: Restructures Dockerfiles for BuildKit layer caching without changing what the image installs, runs, or exposes. A downstream Run step commits and opens the PR.
agents.description: Forked from the Harness dockerfileCacheOptimizer template with MCP connectors optional. The agent only edits Dockerfiles and .dockerignore. Git, branch, and PR work happen in the pipeline Run step. No MCP is required for the happy path.

agents.name: Documentation Generator

agents.description: A technical documentation agent. It discovers structure with Glob, reads entry points, greps public interfaces, and writes generated files marked so later runs can overwrite them without touching hand-written docs.

agents.name: Test Results Summarizer
agents.summary: Turns raw test logs into a concise PASS/FAIL summary with failure list, coverage callouts, and an optional PR comment.
agents.description: Runs after a test step. Reads the test output file, reports totals and failures, and can post or update a PR comment. Designed around go test output but useful anywhere the log is parseable.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: Anthropic or Bedrock connector the agent calls for model access.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model your LLM connector can serve.

configuration.label: Test output file

configuration.label: SCM MCP connector
configuration.note: Only needed to post or update the summary as a pull request comment.

configuration.label: SCM token secret

Optional SCM MCP for PR comments

agents.name: Unit Test Verification
agents.summary: Maps meaningful unit tests to repository services and components, checks a configurable structural coverage threshold, and interrupts the pipeline through Harness MCP when it fails.
agents.description: Analyzes a cloned repository to calculate the percentage of independently testable services and components with meaningful unit tests. It reports its evidence and can use Harness MCP to interrupt the current execution when coverage is below the configured threshold.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: An account, org, or project AI connector available to this project.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model identifier supported by the selected LLM connector.

configuration.label: Harness MCP connector
configuration.note: Must expose the Harness pipeline execution interrupt or abort operation.

configuration.label: Cloned repository
configuration.note: The CI stage must clone the repository into /harness before the agent runs.

configuration.label: Coverage threshold
configuration.note: The percentage of testable services/components that must have meaningful unit tests; defaults to 90.

prerequisites: Harness MCP connector with permission to interrupt pipeline executions

agents.name: Docker Image Tag Inspector
agents.summary: Inspects every tag in a public Docker Hub repository, identifies tags older than a configurable threshold, and recommends cleanup candidates.
agents.description: Queries and paginates the public Docker Hub tags API, calculates exact tag ages, groups stale tags, and reports conservative cleanup and storage recommendations without deleting anything.

configuration.note: Tags older than this many days are reported; defaults to 30.

agents.name: Docker Tag Governance Agent
agents.summary: Evaluates Docker Hub tag retention rules, estimates storage costs, supports approval-gated cleanup, and protects designated release tags.
agents.description: Audits one or more Docker Hub repositories using protected patterns, retain-count, and age rules. It is report-only by default and requires a Docker Hub username and token secret before performing deletions.

agents.name: Incident On-call RCA
agents.summary: Investigates one pinned alert runbook-first across PagerDuty, Confluence, Grafana, Cloud Logging, and Harness deploys, then writes a grounded RCA and opens a fix PR only when the alert is actionable.
agents.description: An advanced multi-provider on-call agent. A first step installs stdio MCP runtimes (Grafana, PagerDuty, harness-mcp-v2), writes provider credentials to files instead of interpolating them into scripts, emits an MCP server config, and optionally sparse-checks out a team skill pack. The agent then triages the single incident in its request payload, prefers the runbook over blind metric queries, bounds every Grafana and gcloud window to the incident, requires an inspected commit diff before claiming a deploy caused the failure, and treats one Harness Code pull request as its only allowed write.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: An Anthropic-backed AI connector. The sub-agent and Skill tooling assume a Claude model today.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model your LLM connector can serve, such as a Claude model id or a Bedrock inference profile ARN.

configuration.label: Atlassian MCP connector
configuration.note: Supplies read-only Confluence and Jira tools for runbooks and known issues. Replace the YOUR_ATLASSIAN_MCP_CONNECTOR placeholder.

configuration.label: Atlassian cloudId
configuration.note: Passed on every Confluence and Jira call. This is an input so no tenant id is committed to the catalog.

configuration.label: PagerDuty API key
configuration.note: A read-scoped User API key. The agent never acknowledges, resolves, or reassigns incidents.

configuration.label: Grafana service-account token
configuration.note: Needed to read alert rules and run bounded Prometheus or Loki queries. Also set grafana_url.

configuration.label: Harness PAT
configuration.note: Used by harness-mcp-v2 for repositories, pull-requests, and pipelines. Needs pull-request create permission for the actionable path.

configuration.label: GCP service-account JSON
configuration.note: Only required when the agent should read Cloud Logging with gcloud. Written to an ADC file with 0600 permissions.

configuration.label: Team skill pack
configuration.note: Optional git repo holding plugin.json plus skills/<name>/SKILL.md for service maps and playbooks. Team skills override the inline steps.

prerequisites: Harness PAT with repository and pull-request access
Grafana token and URL for metric evidence
Optional GCP credentials for Cloud Logging

agents.name: Change Advisory Go/No-Go
agents.summary: Builds a CAB decision for a pending release by reconciling the Harness execution diff, the Confluence CAB runbook, open Jira risks, and a bounded telemetry window.
agents.description: A release governance agent that answers go, hold, or rollback-watch with cited evidence. It inspects the actual commit diff behind an execution or artifact rather than trusting the pipeline name, reads the CAB page for the target service and environment, checks unresolved Jira risks from the last 14 days, and optionally samples RED or error-budget metrics. It holds by default when evidence is incomplete, and it never approves, runs, interrupts, or merges anything.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: An accessible account, org, or project AI connector.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model supported by the selected LLM connector.

configuration.label: Atlassian MCP connector
configuration.note: Read-only Confluence and Jira access for the CAB page and open risks.

configuration.label: CAB Confluence space
configuration.note: Scopes the single CQL search so the agent does not wander across the wiki.

configuration.label: Jira project
configuration.note: Project searched for unresolved risks touching this service in the last 14 days.

configuration.label: Harness PAT
configuration.note: Read access to executions, repositories, and commits. The agent performs no pipeline actions.

configuration.label: Grafana service-account token
configuration.note: Enables the bounded RED or error-budget check. The agent skips telemetry and says so when unmapped.

configuration.label: Change request payload
configuration.note: JSON naming the service, environment, and the pipeline, execution, or artifact under review.

prerequisites: Harness PAT with execution and repository read access
CAB Confluence space and Jira project
Optional Grafana token for telemetry evidence

agents.name: Security Finding Triage
agents.summary: Triages one STO or SCS finding by re-reading the cited file, checking for duplicate Jira issues, and classifying exploitability, with ticket creation and fix PRs behind explicit flags.
agents.description: A security triage agent that reduces scanner noise without silently mutating anything. It fetches the finding through Harness MCP, reads the referenced file at the scan ref to confirm the issue still exists, runs one narrow JQL for similar open issues, and classifies the finding as exploitable, needs-review, or likely false positive. Jira creation happens only when create_ticket is true and no duplicate exists, and a pull request happens only when open_fix_pr is true and the fix is a genuinely one-file, low-risk patch it can name exactly.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: An accessible account, org, or project AI connector.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model supported by the selected LLM connector.

configuration.label: Atlassian MCP connector
configuration.note: Used to search for duplicate issues, and to create one issue when create_ticket is enabled.

configuration.label: Harness PAT
configuration.note: Needs STO and SCS finding read plus repository read. Pull-request create is required only when open_fix_pr is true.

configuration.label: Create Jira ticket
configuration.note: Defaults to false. When true the agent creates at most one issue, and skips creation if a duplicate already exists.

configuration.label: Open fix pull request
configuration.note: Defaults to false. When true the agent still refuses to open a PR unless the patch is one file and low risk.

configuration.label: Owned repositories
configuration.note: Constrains which repositories the agent may read or branch from. It never guesses a repo.

prerequisites: Harness PAT with STO/SCS finding and repository access
Pull-request permission only when open_fix_pr is enabled

agents.name: Runbook Drift Detector
agents.summary: Compares documented runbook alerts, queries, thresholds, and owners against live Grafana rules and Harness pipelines, then reports drift without editing the wiki.
agents.description: A documentation-versus-reality agent for teams whose runbooks quietly rot. It reads a bounded set of Confluence runbook pages, extracts documented alert names, queries, thresholds, owners, and pipeline names, and marks whether each was quoted or inferred. It then fetches the live Grafana rules and named Harness pipelines and reports missing-in-prod, missing-in-docs, stale-query, and broken-link findings. It never edits Confluence or changes alert rules, and it can open a single docs pull request when explicitly enabled.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: An accessible account, org, or project AI connector.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model supported by the selected LLM connector.

configuration.label: Atlassian MCP connector
configuration.note: Read-only Confluence access. The agent is explicitly forbidden from editing pages.

configuration.label: Grafana folder or rule UIDs
configuration.note: Bounds which alert rules are compared. Prevents whole-instance scans and full dashboard JSON reads.

configuration.label: Harness pipeline ids
configuration.note: The documented pipelines to compare against real stages and steps.

configuration.label: Open docs pull request
configuration.note: Defaults to false. When true the agent writes a drift report to docs_repo_id on its own branch.

configuration.label: Docs repository
configuration.note: Required only when open_docs_pr is true. Must be a team-owned repository.

configuration.label: Grafana service-account token
configuration.note: Read access to alerting rules. Also set grafana_url.

prerequisites: Grafana token with alert rule read access
Harness PAT with pipeline read access
Docs repository only when open_docs_pr is enabled

agents.name: Incident Customer Comms Drafter
agents.summary: Drafts separate internal and customer-safe incident updates from the pinned PagerDuty incident, a bounded impact window, and your Confluence status template.
agents.description: A comms drafting agent for the moment when engineers are busy and customers are waiting. It reads only the pinned PagerDuty incident, follows your Confluence status-page template, and optionally confirms the impact window in Grafana. It produces two clearly separated blocks so a human can review before anything is sent, and customer text is explicitly barred from hostnames, IPs, stack traces, and internal channel names. It never mutates PagerDuty, never pages anyone, and never publishes a status page.

configuration.label: LLM connector
configuration.note: An accessible account, org, or project AI connector.

configuration.label: Model id
configuration.note: A model supported by the selected LLM connector.

configuration.label: Atlassian MCP connector
configuration.note: Read-only access used to fetch the status-page template page.

configuration.label: Confluence status template
configuration.note: Page id or title. The drafted sections follow this template rather than an invented format.

configuration.label: PagerDuty API key
configuration.note: Read-scoped. The agent investigates only the pinned incident and performs no PagerDuty writes.

configuration.label: Severity
configuration.note: Drives tone and update cadence. Team skills can define approved language per severity.

configuration.label: Grafana service-account token
configuration.note: Used only to confirm the impact window. The agent skips this and says so when unmapped.

configuration.label: Include customer draft in Slack post
configuration.note: Defaults to false. Even when true the pipeline only posts to Slack, never to a public status page.

prerequisites: Optional Grafana token for impact confirmation
